chunks: ʿAlī narrated from his father, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

If two witr prayers, or three, or more than that have accumulated upon you, then make them up as they were missed. You separate between every two witr prayers with a salat (prayer). Do not place anything before the first of them; begin with the first, then the first in order. When you make up the prayer of your night, then the witr.
He said: And Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: “There are not two witr prayers in one night except that one of them is a make-up.”

And he said: “If you performed witr in the first part of the night and then rose in the last part of the night, then your first witr is a make-up. Whatever salat (prayer) you perform during that entire night, let it be make-up until the end of your prayer, for it belongs to your night; and let the last of your prayer be the witr of your night.”

key_terms.تَفْصِلُ: you separate one set from another
key_terms.صَلَاةَ لَيْلَتِكَ: the night prayer belonging to that night
key_terms.فَاقْضِ: perform as qada'; make up what was missed
key_terms.قَضَاءٌ: a make-up performance of a missed act of worship
key_terms.لَا وَتْرَانِ فِي لَيْلَةٍ: there are not two witr prayers as current performance in one night

ai.seo_question: How should multiple missed witr prayers be made up, and can there be two witr prayers in one night?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling for making up multiple missed witr prayers and maintaining their proper order. It also clarifies that two witr prayers are not combined as two current prayers in one night; rather, one is treated as qada', and the final prayer of the night should be its witr.
